claim: A `jump <label> ...` whose label is not defined anywhere in the program is not a jump to -1: LParser.parse() throws "Invalid code. Undefined jump location", LAssembler.read() propagates it, and LogicBlock.updateCode() catches it by loading an EMPTY program -- the whole processor stops running, every statement is lost, not just this jump.
why: LParser.java:130-133 records the label name and rewrites the operand to -1 only so the line can be parsed; :181-202 then walks the jump table and calls error("Undefined jump location: ... Make sure the jump label exists and is typed correctly.") for any label missing from jumpLocations, which throws a RuntimeException out of parse(). LAssembler.java:53-57 does not catch it, so it reaches LogicBlock.java:430-432, whose catch reloads the executor with `LAssembler.assemble(code = "", privileged)` -- an empty program, i.e. the processor goes idle. Real-engine probes (out/_noop_matrix2.py) confirm: `set x 1` + `jump nope always` throws before executing, and label case matters (`start:` with `jump Start` throws too). This is not the -1 fall-through the old WARN message claimed.
